transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, I really hope I'm not wasting your time—it's probably nothing major, honestly. But I guess I came in because I've just been feeling pretty worn out almost every day. 

Like, even after a full night's sleep, my body and my head are just dragging when I get up for my cashier shift. I always try my best to push through it at work, I don't want to complain or be a bad employee or anything, but... yeah, it's just been a little hard to shake lately. Is that... does that make sense for why I'd come see you?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um, let's see... I guess it's been about a year and three months? Give or take. It's not like it's been unbearable the whole time, I really don't want to sound like I'm just whining about it. 

But I think I started noticing it right around the time our, um... our older relative moved in with us. We had to adjust some things at home, which is totally fine, I'm happy to help family, you know? It's just a bit of an adjustment. But yeah, about a year and a few months. Is that... does that answer your question okay?
Have you noticed any changes in how much you enjoy the things you used to like doing?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I still like doing all the normal stuff I usually do. Like, I still watch TV and, you know, try to relax when I get home. I don't think I've lost interest or anything like that. I really try to stay positive and appreciate the little things, you know? I definitely wouldn't say I'm depressed or anything, if that's what you mean. I still enjoy my life, I just... I just get a little tired sometimes. Does that sound normal to you?
Do you often feel sad?

No, no, I wouldn't say I feel sad. I mean, everyone has their moments, right? But generally, I'm a pretty upbeat guy. I really try to look on the bright side of things. I know I said I was tired, but I don't want you to think I'm sitting around crying or feeling sorry for myself or anything like that. I'm just... you know, trying to keep everything running smoothly. I hope I'm not giving you the wrong impression?
Do you often feel anxious or worried?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? But I think it's just normal stuff, really. I definitely don't want to make a big deal out of it. It just feels like my mind is kind of always jumping from one thing to the next. 

Like, I'll be thinking about money, and then making sure everything is going okay with the relative staying with us, and then I start worrying about my wife being stressed out. And then there's my church duties, and... and just hoping I'm not messing up at work, you know, at the store. I just really want to do a good job and be responsible for everyone. It's not like I'm having breakdowns or anything like that. Just... trying to keep on top of it all. Is it normal to think about all that stuff so much? I hope I'm answering your question right.
Are there things that you used to enjoy doing, but no longer find pleasure in?

No, no, definitely not. I think... I think maybe you asked me something similar a minute ago? But yeah, I still really enjoy all the things I usually do. I haven't lost interest in anything at all. Like I said, I still like watching TV and just relaxing with my wife when we have the time. I'm really trying to keep a good attitude about everything, you know? I definitely don't want you to think I'm losing my spark or anything like that. I'm still the same guy, just... just a little busy right now. I hope that makes sense?
Do you find yourself getting irritated or short-tempered more often than you used to?

Oh, um, no. No, I wouldn't say that at all. I really try my best to be patient with everyone. Working as a cashier, you know, you kind of have to learn to just smile and let things roll off your back, right? 

And at home, I'd hate for anyone to think I'm snapping at my wife or anything like that. I really just try to keep the peace and make sure everyone is happy. Even when my mind is racing with all that stuff I mentioned, I just keep it to myself. I definitely don't take it out on other people. I hope I'm not coming across as angry or difficult? I really try to be easy to get along with.
Have you been having any trouble sleeping?

Well, um... maybe just a little? I mean, I definitely don't want to complain, and it's really not that bad. Most nights I do get in bed feeling pretty tired, ready to sleep. But then... I don't know, I just lie there for a while. My mind just starts going over the bills, or my work schedule for the week, and just trying to make sure everyone at home is okay. 

And I guess... even when I do finally get to sleep, I tend to wake up feeling like I never really, you know, settled down. But I still get up and make it to my shift on time every day! I'm definitely not letting it stop me from doing what I need to do. That's just a normal part of being an adult with responsibilities, right? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it actually is.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite?

Oh, no, my appetite is totally fine. I'm still eating just like I always do. I mean, my wife is a great cook, so I always make sure to eat whatever she makes. I'd never want her to think I don't appreciate her cooking, you know? So yeah, breakfast, lunch, dinner—everything is pretty much the same as it's always been. I haven't lost any weight or anything. I'm staying healthy, I promise! Is it okay that my appetite hasn't changed? I hope that's a good sign.
Do you have trouble focusing or paying attention to things?

Well, um... I guess maybe sometimes? But really, I try my hardest to stay focused, especially at work. I know how important it is to be accurate at the register. 

It's just... sometimes, I'll be looking right at the screen, and my mind just sort of drifts off to, you know, things at home or worrying about the bills. And then I might lose track for a second. I've had to recount the drawer a couple of times, or, you know, catch a small mistake before it became a big deal. But I always catch it! I really pride myself on doing a good job. I hope my boss doesn't think I'm slacking off or anything. It's normal to get a little distracted when you have a lot on your mind, right? I mean, I'm still doing my job well, I promise.
Have you experienced any physical symptoms like headaches or muscle tension?

Oh, physical symptoms? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, my head feels fine, and I'm not, like, in pain or anything. Sometimes my shoulders get a little stiff after standing at the register all day, but that's just from working hard, you know? Anyone would get a little sore from being on their feet for an eight-hour shift. 

I definitely don't have any major headaches or anything that would keep me from doing my job or helping out at home. I make sure to stretch a little bit, and I'm good to go! So physically, I think I'm doing really well. I'm taking good care of myself, I promise. That's what you're looking for, right?
Do you often feel guilty about things?

Guilty? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I always try my hardest to do the right thing, you know? Whether I'm ringing people up at the store or helping out at home with my wife, I just... I really try to be dependable. 

So there isn't really much for me to feel guilty about, because I make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing. If I ever do mess up a little, I apologize and fix it right away! I never want anyone to think I'm letting them down or not pulling my weight. So, no, no real guilt or anything like that. I'm just doing my best to be a good guy. That's... that's a good thing, right? I hope I'm answering these okay for you.
Do you find yourself having thoughts that keep repeating in your mind?

Repeating thoughts? Um... well, I wouldn't call it like, an obsession or anything bad like that. I just... I like to be prepared, you know? So I guess my mind does kind of jump around a bit sometimes. 

It's just that there's a lot to keep track of right now. Like, making sure the bills are paid, and we have a relative staying with us right now, which is great, but it's just an extra thing to think about. And my wife has been a little stressed, plus I have things I help out with at church, and then, of course, just wanting to make sure I'm doing a perfect job at work. 

So, yeah, my brain just sort of hops from one thing to the next, just trying to make sure I don't drop the ball on anything. It's just me being responsible, I think. A lot of people probably think about those kinds of things throughout the day, right? It just means I care about taking care of my family and my job. That's normal, isn't it?
Are there things you used to look forward to that you no longer get excited about?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I still really enjoy things! I still look forward to, you know, watching the game on the weekends or having a nice dinner with my wife. I'm definitely not sitting around moping or losing interest in stuff. 

I try to keep a really positive attitude about everything. Even with work and the bills and all that, I always make sure to find time to just be happy. I'd hate for you to think I'm just some kind of downer. I really do try my best to stay upbeat and keep things fun for everyone around me. I think it's important to keep your spirits up, don't you?
Do you often find yourself worrying about things even when there's no obvious reason to worry?

Worrying for no reason? Um... well, I wouldn't say there's *no* reason. I mean, there's always something to be a little concerned about, right? But... I guess sometimes it does get a little hard to turn off. 

I really try not to let it get to me. I'll tell myself to just pray on it, you know, give it to God, or just try to leave it alone and focus on something else. But... sometimes, once a thought starts, it just kind of... keeps rolling. Like, one little worry turns into another one, and before I know it, I'm sort of thinking through every single bad way the day could possibly go. 

It's not that I want to think like that! I really try to be positive, like I said. It's just my brain trying to make sure I'm prepared for anything that could happen. That's just being careful, I think. A lot of people probably do that, right? Just running through the possibilities to make sure everything turns out okay? I hope that makes sense.
Would you say your worrying is mild, moderate, or severe most of the time?

Oh, um... definitely mild. Yeah, very mild. I really wouldn't want you to think it's severe or, you know, out of control or anything like that. I can still ring people up at the register just fine and take care of everything at home. 

It's really just a little bit of extra thinking in the background sometimes. Nothing I can't handle! I think it's just a very normal, mild amount of concern. Everyone has that, right? So, yeah, I'd say it's on the very low end. Does that sound okay?
Does your worrying ever interfere with your daily activities or relationships?

Oh, no, I wouldn't use a word like interfere. I mean, I still get everything done! I'm definitely still holding my own. 

I guess... well, at work, I've been having to double-check my cash drawer a little more often lately. I just made a couple of really small mistakes, nothing major at all, but I want to make absolutely sure my drawer is perfect for my manager. So I just count it an extra time or two. That's just being a good employee, really, making sure everything is right. 

And... um, I did decide to cut back a little on my volunteering at the food pantry. I just... I didn't feel like I could quite keep up with everything right now, so I thought it was best to step back just a bit. But I still do all my regular stuff! Taking a little break from volunteering when you're busy is a pretty normal thing to do, right? I just try to do my best so I don't let anyone down. Does that make sense?
Does your worrying affect how well you can focus on your tasks at work or at home?

Well, um... I wouldn't say it really *affects* my focus in a bad way. I mean, I'm still getting everything done, like I said. But... I guess sometimes my mind just sort of wanders a little bit? 

Like, at the register, I can be looking right at the screen, ringing someone up, and I'll just kind of... lose track for a second. Just because I'm thinking about things at home, or maybe running through my bills in my head, just trying to stay on top of things, you know? And I guess... well, that's usually when I might make one of those little mistakes I mentioned, or why I end up having to recount my drawer. 

It's really nothing major, though! Just a little bit of multitasking in my head, I suppose. I mean, everyone gets a little distracted sometimes when they have responsibilities to think about, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job, so I hope that doesn't sound like I'm not paying attention at work. Does that sound like a normal thing to happen?
Have you noticed any significant problems in your relationships or work performance because of your worrying?

Oh, significant problems? No, no, definitely not. I mean, my manager hasn't said anything bad to me, and my wife and I get along just fine. I try really hard to make sure everything stays smooth, you know? 

I guess... well, my wife did mention the other day that I seem a little quiet sometimes when we're watching TV. But I'm just thinking about stuff, making sure I have everything planned out for the week. It's not a problem or anything, just... me trying to be responsible. And at work, like I said, just those tiny little slip-ups with the drawer, but I always catch them myself. That's not a significant problem, is it? I feel like I'm still doing a really good job overall.
How long have you been worrying like this?

Well, um... I guess it's been a little while now. Maybe about a year and three months? Give or take? 

It really kind of started when my wife's older relative had to move in with us. Which is totally fine, of course! We're happy to have them, and it's just what family does, right? It just added a few more things to my plate, you know, figuring out the space and the extra groceries and all that. So I just started thinking ahead a little more, making sure everything was taken care of for everyone. 

It's just a normal adjustment period, really. A year and a bit isn't that long when you think about a big life change like that, is it? I just want to make sure I'm doing right by my family.
